title: Large language models
description: The models behind many AI chats. They learn patterns in language and generate responses a piece at a time.
exercise: Ask for an explanation using a hobby you love. Then explain it back in your own words.

title: Prompts & context
description: A prompt is what you ask. Context is the background that helps the model understand what you mean.
exercise: Give it a goal, a real example and what a good answer looks like. Compare that with a one-line ask.

title: Tokens & context windows
description: Tokens are small pieces of text. A context window is how much information a model can work with in one response.
exercise: Ask why a long chat can lose the thread. Try a short recap before your next request.

title: Hallucinations & fact-checking
description: AI can give a confident answer that is wrong—even an invented quote or source. Fluency is not proof.
exercise: Pick one factual claim from a chat. Open the original source and see if it actually supports the claim.

title: Multimodal AI
description: Some models work with more than text, such as images or audio. What you can use depends on the tool.
exercise: Try a photo of your own notes. Ask for a summary, then check what it missed.

title: ChatGPT
description: A place to practice thinking with AI. Start with one real task and a conversation, rather than a perfect prompt.
exercise: Bring a small decision you are stuck on. Ask it to interview you before suggesting an answer.

title: Claude
description: Another AI assistant to try for writing, thinking and building. Comparing answers can help you notice what you value.
exercise: Give it the same small task as another assistant. Compare usefulness, tone and what each gets wrong.

title: NotebookLM / Gemini Notebook
description: Google’s research notebook lets you work with sources you choose and follow citations back to them.
exercise: Add two sources on a question you care about. Ask where they agree and disagree, then open the citations.

title: Projects & reusable instructions
description: Keep related chats, files and instructions together so you do not have to explain the same project from scratch.
exercise: Make a project for one recurring task. Add your goals and an example of work you like.

title: tldraw & visual thinking
description: A whiteboard for sketching ideas and diagrams. Mary’s starting point: make the explanation something you can see.
exercise: Sketch a process you already know. Use an AI assistant to help simplify the steps, then redraw it.

title: Agents & workflows
description: A workflow follows a planned sequence. An agent can choose steps and use tools as it works toward a goal.
exercise: Map one task into steps. Which should be fixed, which need judgment, and where should you review?

title: Skills & tool connections
description: Skills package reusable instructions or resources. Tool connections let an assistant work with another app.
exercise: Choose one repeated task. Write the instructions and list the apps it would need access to.

title: Build one useful thing
description: Our challenge: choose a small, real problem and practice solving it with AI. The win is usefulness, not complexity.
exercise: Pick one annoying task this week. Define what “done” means before asking AI to build anything.

title: A learning routine that sticks
description: Our suggestion: a short list of sources, a vocabulary list and a format you enjoy. You do not need every update.
exercise: Choose three unfamiliar terms. Ask for an analogy, explain them back and revisit them next week.

title: Privacy & your data
description: Before connecting an app or sharing a file, understand what data is involved and which controls you have.
exercise: Choose a tool you use. Read its data controls and decide what you are comfortable putting into it.

title: AI, energy & the environment
description: What does AI use, what might it save, and which trade-offs depend on how and where it is deployed?
exercise: Read the IEA overview. Separate what is measured today from what is a forecast.

title: AI & the future of your work
description: Go deeper on the questions that matter to your own industry, role or next career move.
exercise: List three tasks in your work. Which might change, and what evidence would help you judge?

title: AGI & measuring progress
description: A big question worth unpacking: what would broadly capable AI mean, and how would we know we were getting there?
exercise: Compare two definitions. Write down what each would count as evidence and what it leaves out.
